title: ConfidentStochasticSurjectiveInequalities.lean

problem_class.label: nonconvex
problem_class.details: Minimize differentiable f(x) subject to m nonlinear inequalities c_i(x)≤0 in a finite-dimensional real inner-product space. Neither f nor the constraints must be convex.

oracle.label: stochastic_gradient
oracle.details: Each call queries two points x,y and returns objective-gradient, constraint-value, and constraint-Jacobian estimates at both points using the same sample. Samples across calls are IID. All three estimates are unbiased; objective values are not supplied.

oracle.label: function_value
oracle.details: The oracle supplies noisy values of the entire constraint vector at each queried point, jointly with derivative estimates.

distinctive_assumptions.label: bounded_variance
distinctive_assumptions.details: Uniformly in x, the sum of expected squared errors of the objective gradient, constraint values, and constraint Jacobian is at most σ². No exponential-tail assumption is imposed.

distinctive_assumptions.label: finite_dimensional
distinctive_assumptions.details: E is a finite-dimensional real inner-product space with its Borel measurable structure; constraints lie in R^m.

distinctive_assumptions.label: other
distinctive_assumptions.details: For all x and multipliers ℓ, ‖ℓ‖≤H‖J(x)^Tℓ‖. Objective gradients and Jacobians have norm at most H and are H-Lipschitz. The same-sample sum of squared differences of all three oracle outputs has expectation at most H²‖x−y‖². The penalty F(x)=f(x)+4H(H+1)Σ_i max(c_i(x),0) satisfies F(x0)−F(x)≤Δ for every x. Public parameters include E, Ω, m, H, σ, Δ, ε, x0, δ; f,c,J and the sampling law are hidden. Restrictions: m>0, H≥1, σ,Δ≥0, 0<ε≤1, 0<δ<1.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/StochasticSurjectiveInequalities.lean: Regularity, OracleConditions.meanSquaredSmooth, penalty, spec.Public/Instance/valid/admissible; LongTails/Setups/ConfidentStochasticSurjectiveInequalities.lean: Params, spec.Public/publicInput/valid.

accuracy.label: feasibility
accuracy.details: The Euclidean norm of the positive part of c(x) must satisfy ‖[c(x)]_+‖₂≤ε at the returned point.

accuracy.label: high_probability
accuracy.details: All accuracy conditions must hold simultaneously with probability at least 1−δ under the joint algorithm and oracle randomness, using a fixed cap on paired oracle calls.

accuracy.label: other
accuracy.details: Return a measurable pair (x,λ) with λ_i≥0, ‖∇f(x)+J(x)^Tλ‖≤ε, and Σ_i|λ_i c_i(x)|≤ε, jointly with the feasibility requirement.

setup_category.label: non_standard
setup_category.reason: The nonlinear stochastic inequality formulation combines global uniform Jacobian surjectivity, bounded derivatives, jointly mean-square smooth paired oracle outputs, and a simultaneous high-probability primal-dual KKT guarantee.

descriptionHtml:
Stochastic Inequalities with Surjective Jacobians

We consider minimizing a differentiable function f:E→R subject to ci(x)≤0, where E is a finite-dimensional real inner product space and ci:E→R, i=1,…,m, are differentiable constraints. Gradients are bounded and Lipschitz, the constraint Jacobian is uniformly surjective, and the initial penalty gap is bounded. Each oracle call returns unbiased estimates of the objective gradient, constraint values, and constraint gradients at two points using a shared sample; samples across calls are independent, with bounded variance and mean-square smoothness. Given ε∈(0,1] and δ∈(0,1), the goal is a pair (x¯,λ¯)∈E×R+m satisfying ∥∇f(x¯)+∑iλ¯i∇ci(x¯)∥≤ε, ∥(max{ci(x¯),0})i∥≤ε, and ∑i|λ¯ici(x¯)|≤ε simultaneously with probability at least 1−δ.

The optimization problem is minx∈E: ci(x)≤0, i=1,…,mf(x). Write c=(c1,…,cm):E→Rm and J(x)=(∇ci(x))i=1m∈Em,J(x)⊤λ=∑i=1mλi∇ci(x),λ∈Rm. The norm on E is induced by its inner product; Rm, Em, and their products carry Euclidean product norms. In particular, ∥J(x)∥2=∑i∥∇ci(x)∥2. The parameters satisfy m≥1,H≥1,σ≥0,Δ≥0,0<ε≤1,0<δ<1. The algorithm receives E, a measurable sample space Ω, m, H, σ, Δ, ε, δ, and a given starting point x0∈E.

Our assumptions:

Assumption 1 (Regularity and surjectivity). The functions f and ci are Fréchet differentiable everywhere. For every x,y∈E and λ∈Rm, ∥∇f(x)∥≤H,∥J(x)∥≤H,∥∇f(x)−∇f(y)∥≤H∥x−y∥,∥J(x)−J(y)∥≤H∥x−y∥,∥λ∥≤H∥J(x)⊤λ∥.

Assumption 2 (Initial penalty gap). Define the penalty function Φ(x)=f(x)+4H(H+1)∑i=1mmax{ci(x),0}. The given point x0 satisfies Φ(x0)−Φ(x)≤Δfor every x∈E.

Assumption 3 (Stochastic estimates). There is a probability law ν on Ω and jointly measurable maps g:E×Ω→E,v:E×Ω→Rm,D:E×Ω→Em. Set F(x,ξ)=(g(x,ξ),v(x,ξ),D(x,ξ)),T(x)=(∇f(x),c(x),J(x)). For every fixed x∈E, the three components of F(x,⋅) are Bochner integrable under ν, and Eξ∼ν[F(x,ξ)]=T(x). For every x,y∈E, the random variables ∥F(x,ξ)−T(x)∥2 and ∥F(x,ξ)−F(y,ξ)∥2 are integrable and satisfy Eξ∼ν[∥F(x,ξ)−T(x)∥2]≤σ2,Eξ∼ν[∥F(x,ξ)−F(y,ξ)∥2]≤H2∥x−y∥2.

A query is any pair (x,y)∈E×E. At call k, the oracle returns (F(x,ξk),F(y,ξk)). The samples (ξk)k≥0 are measurable, mutually independent, and each has law ν. They are independent of the algorithm’s randomness. Thus one call provides both triples using the same sample, including when the query points are chosen adaptively.

After the allotted calls, the algorithm must return a measurable pair (x¯,λ¯)∈E×Rm. Define c+(x)=(max{ci(x),0})i=1m. The required accuracy is P(λ¯∈R+m,∥∇f(x¯)+J(x¯)⊤λ¯∥≤ε,∥c+(x¯)∥≤ε,∑i=1m|λ¯ici(x¯)|≤ε)≥1−δ, where P is the joint law of the algorithm’s randomness and the oracle samples.

comparisonHtml:
Minimize f(x) subject to c(x)≤0 on a finite-dimensional real inner-product space. Globally, ∥∇f∥,∥J∥F,Lip(∇f),Lip(J)≤H and ∥λ∥≤H∥J(x)∗λ∥ for every x,λ, including inactive rows. The penalty F=f+4H(H+1)∑i[ci]+ satisfies F(x0)−infF≤Δ. Jointly measurable, integrable stochastic triples (g,v,D) have means (∇f,c,J), summed mean-square error at most σ2, and summed same-sample mean-square differences at most H2∥x−y∥2. Samples are IID under an abstract probability law P. Here m≥1, H≥1, Δ,σ≥0, 0<ε≤1, 0<δ<1. Target: a measurable pair (x,λ) with P{λ≥0, ∥∇f(x)+J(x)∗λ∥≤ε, ∥[c(x)]+∥≤ε, ∑i|λici(x)|≤ε}≥1−δ.

Comparison for ConfidentStochasticSurjectiveInequalities.
Result Oracle complexity Novelty Limitations
(1) ConfidentSurjectiveStochasticInequalityKkt (Ours) (⋆⋆⋆) (review) O(ℓ[1+m2H10Δε2+m4H19Δσε3]+ℓ2[1+m4H18σ2ε2]) paired triple calls, including replication and validation.
(2) Prox-linear (Zhang and Xiao 2021), Thm. 3; hinge-penalty specialization O(ε−5) total joint calls; values O(ε−5), Jacobians O(ε−3). Fixed remaining parameters; E∥GM∥2≤ε2. KKT conversion uses surjectivity. (1): Values ε−5→ε−3 for fixed positive m,H,Δ,σ and ℓ=o(ε−2). Explicit complementary KKT pair with confidence 1−δ, replacing expected prox-gradient accuracy. (1) requires global surjectivity, hence m≤dim⁡E; (2) permits broader composite objectives.
(3) Directional decomposition (Shi and Wang 2025), Thm. 7; bounded-constraint, level-bounded-objective, sample-smooth subclass O(ε−5(1+log⁡(1/ε))2) total calls; gradient/Jacobian calls O(ε−3(1+log⁡(1/ε))2). Fixed remaining parameters; KKT confidence 1−ε. (1): Value exponent 5→3 on the common subclass, fixed positive remaining parameters and ℓ=o(ε−2). Arbitrary δ; finite variance and mean-square smoothness replace bounded errors and sample-wise smoothness. No bounded c or level-bounded f required. (1) requires globally surjective whole Jacobians; (3) allows redundant rows and m>dim⁡E through slack-form strong MFCQ. Classes are incomparable.

Abbr: J=Dc; m is the constraint count; [⋅]+ is componentwise positive part; ℓ=1+log⁡(1/δ). One paired call evaluates (g,v,D) at two points with one fresh common sample; single-point primitive counts differ by universal factors. GM is the exact prox-linear gradient mapping. Prior-work constants are not mapped to m,H,Δ,σ.

Shi, Qiankun, and Xiao Wang. 2025. Adaptive Directional Decomposition Methods for Nonconvex Constrained Optimization. https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2511.03210.
Zhang, Junyu, and Lin Xiao. 2021. Stochastic Variance-Reduced Prox-Linear Algorithms for Nonconvex Composite Optimization. https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2004.04357.

import LongTails.Setups.StochasticSurjectiveInequalities

open MeasureTheory

namespace LongTails.Setups.ConfidentStochasticSurjectiveInequalities

open OracleTemplate

structure Params where
  problem : StochasticSurjectiveInequalities.Params
  δ : ℝ

abbrev spec : Setup where
  Params := Params
  Public := Params
  Instance p := StochasticSurjectiveInequalities.Problem p.problem
  Query p := p.problem.E × p.problem.E
  Reply p := StochasticSurjectiveInequalities.Primitive p.problem ×
    StochasticSurjectiveInequalities.Primitive p.problem
  Output p := p.problem.E × StochasticSurjectiveInequalities.Constraint p.problem
  publicInput p := p
  valid p := StochasticSurjectiveInequalities.spec.valid p.problem ∧ 0 < p.δ ∧ p.δ < 1
  admissible p := StochasticSurjectiveInequalities.spec.admissible p.problem
  successful p I output P := Measurable output ∧
    ENNReal.ofReal (1 - p.δ) ≤
      (P : Measure _) {ω | StochasticSurjectiveInequalities.accurate p.problem I (output ω)}

end LongTails.Setups.ConfidentStochasticSurjectiveInequalities
